final_message:
**Status:** Reproduced

**Expected:** `type Test = { prop1: "hello"; }`, as on 5.6.3.

**Actual:** `type Test = { prop1: Wrapper<"hello">; }` on this checkout (5.8.0-dev, 6b1ea96) and on 5.7.2. Hover (quick info) and error messages show the same text.

**Trigger:** The property `prop1: stringWrapper() as Wrapper<"hello">` is an inline `as` assertion in the object literal passed to `objWrapper`. Hoisting the assertion into its own `const` (the report's workaround) prints `{ prop1: "hello"; }` on all three versions. It looks like a display problem rather than a wrong type. The checker's type for `prop1` is `"hello"`, `Test["prop1"]` rejects `5` as not assignable to `"hello"`, and `{ prop1: "hello" }` is assignable from `Test`. Only the printed text is wrong. The same wrong text is emitted into declaration files. With `--declaration`, `export function f(): { [K in keyof Test]: Test[K] }` followed by `export const g = f();` emits `g: { prop1: Wrapper<"hello"> }` on this checkout and `{ prop1: "hello" }` on 5.6.3.

**Run:** `node recreate/check.js` from the repo root. It builds the report's exact code (`recreate/wrapper-assertion.ts`) with `built/local/typescript.js`, prints the type of `Test`, and exits 1 unless it is `{ prop1: "hello"; }`. Set `TS_PATH=<path to typescript.js>` to test another compiler.

**Passes when:** `TS_PATH=<5.6.3 install>/node_modules/typescript/lib/typescript.js node recreate/check.js` prints `{ prop1: "hello"; }` and exits 0. The same command with 5.7.2 fails the same way as this checkout.

**Artifacts:** `recreate/check.js` and `recreate/wrapper-assertion.ts` in the repo working tree. Nothing else was added.

No production code was changed.
